name: What are common hidden problems found during commercial renovations?

mainEntity.name: What hidden problems are most often found during commercial renovations in older buildings?
mainEntity.text: What hidden problems are most often found during commercial renovations in older buildings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hidden conditions are one of the biggest risks in commercial renovations, especially in older buildings. Once finishes are removed, contractors often discover outdated wiring, undersized plumbing, damaged framing, previous unpermitted modifications, water intrusion, or uneven surfaces that were not visible during the estimate. In some projects, older materials or concealed building components can also require extra testing or specialized handling. These surprises can affect budget, permit scope, and schedule all at once. The best defense is a thorough preconstruction review and a contingency plan that assumes at least some unknowns. Owners should also avoid using a minimal allowance when the building has a long history of repairs or tenant turnover. In commercial work, hidden problems are normal enough that the contract and schedule should be written with flexibility. The goal is not to eliminate surprises entirely, but to identify them early and handle them without losing control of the project.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common hidden problems include damaged framing, outdated electrical, undersized plumbing, water intrusion, uneven slabs, and unapproved prior work. Demolition may also reveal asbestos-related concerns, poor patchwork repairs, or mismatched systems. These issues usually affect budget, schedule, and permit scope.
